references.text: This text tells the original account of the victory over Sihon, king of the Amorites in Heshbon, and Og, king of Bashan. Deuteronomy 1:4 refers back to these events.
Moses gives a more detailed account of the defeat of Sihon, king of the Amorites who lived in Heshbon, which is also mentioned in Deuteronomy 1:4.
Here an expanded account is given of the victory over Og, king of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth and Edrei, the same places mentioned in Deuteronomy 1:4.
Moses reminds the people of the victory over Sihon and Og, confirming the historical events mentioned in Deuteronomy 1:4.
The Lord uses the victory over Sihon and Og as an example of how He will help Israel against their enemies.
Joshua mentions Og, king of Bashan, who lived in Ashtaroth and Edrei, the same places mentioned in Deuteronomy 1:4.
The text describes the territory of Sihon and Og, confirming the geographical details from Deuteronomy 1:4 about Heshbon, Ashtaroth, and Edrei.
The Levites praise God in their prayer and mention the victory over Sihon, king of Heshbon, and Og, king of Bashan.
The psalm praises the Lord for striking down Sihon, king of the Amorites, as mentioned in Deuteronomy 1:4.
